limits_and_disagreements: Installed atomscan embeds a stale validator missing the documented metadata/file/naming 101-rule allowance. Comparison scans consistently use CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 with --no-update --mode slow --follow=none; final validation uses the newer source-tree release with full checks.
Atomscan reports feature spec v18 against extractor v19. Raw model probability and calibration level are recorded verbatim rather than interpreted as proof of intent.

The Python package explicitly identifies itself as an authorized pentest probe in source and project description. This does not prove deployment authorization. Its actual diagnostic callback matches that purpose, with no credential values, persistence or payload execution. The accurate hostile install-time OOB callback and suspicious identity transmission remain despite the BENIGN verdict.

The JavaScript comment describes credential extraction and GitHub-issue export, but no execution path reaches it. Only console.log executes; no package lifecycle hook runs it. The tsc bin alias and sparse recent package metadata are cautionary context, not proof of hostile effects.

The macOS next-stage response was not recovered or executed. Its privileged-looking identity, hidden login execution, attacker-controlled AppleScript compilation/launch, telemetry and cleanup establish malicious behavior without knowing the final tasks.
No fetched dependency caused these findings; neither archive declares a runtime dependency requiring isolated PURL correction.
